answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may post offers, then slash that stake when a dispute proves fraud. Splitting one operator across many identities no longer creates influence for free: every account ties up capital, and each fake must survive independent checks and risk losing its bond. A dune-based market map, an atlas of counterparties, or a crystal-clear reputation record can help expose linked behavior, but the binding cost is capital at risk, not a promise that identity checks are perfect.
